text_input: 55-year-old male presented with generalized weakness and fatigue for one year. He has a history of iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome due to prolonged steroid use (Diclofenac and Dexamethasone) prescribed by an ayurvedic doctor. Known comorbidities include Ischemic Heart Disease (8 years), Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (7-8 years), and Hypertension (6 years). Physical examination showed moon-like facies, purple striae, and a buffalo hump. Laboratory investigations revealed a WBC count of 19,830 cells/µL, Hemoglobin of 12.0 g/dL, and HbA1c of 8.9%. Urine analysis showed significant pyuria (leucocytes ++, PC 20), indicating a Urinary Tract Infection. Imaging showed hepatomegaly with fatty infiltration and an umbilical hernia. 2D Echo showed an ejection fraction of 55% with left ventricular diastolic dysfunction and concentric LVH. The patient was managed with insulin, antibiotics (Microtaz), and a tapering dose of steroids (Hisone) under the guidance of an endocrinologist.
